turns.assessment: The alarm originates at oms.S17-S18.amp2, whose input power and pump current stayed unchanged while its output fell by about 8.17 dB. The same loss appears at every downstream amplifier and across all monitored channels at S18, with broad downstream OSNR and BER degradation. This localizes the fault to a gain drop in amp2; tilt, pump failure, span loss, and noise-figure rise do not fit the uniform output-power loss pattern.

proposals.rationale: Stable input with an approximately 8.17 dB output reduction directly indicates lost gain in amp2. The loss propagates unchanged through amp3, amp4, and all S18 channel-power measurements, while downstream OSNR and BER worsen.
A tilt fault could weaken part of the spectrum, but the observations show a nearly uniform loss across all monitored channels and a large aggregate output drop.
A pump failure is strongly contradicted by unchanged pump current and the presence of reduced, rather than absent, output.
